question: Should OpenClaw accept this deny-over-allow exec approval overlay, including `tools.exec.denylist` and `exec-approvals.json` denylists, as the native security-policy shape for this release?
rationale: The PR changes a host-command security boundary and persisted operator config/protocol behavior, so automation can review implementation quality but should not make the product/security acceptance decision.

options.title: Accept after docs and checks
options.body: Require public docs, a clean exact-head check run, and maintainer security acceptance, then continue with this overlay design.

options.title: Narrow the first release
options.body: Limit the merged surface to the smallest accepted config/protocol layer and remove claims for behavior that maintainers do not want to support yet.

options.title: Pause for policy design
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open while maintainers decide denylist mode, prompt-versus-hard-deny semantics, UI exposure, and overlap with path-deny work.

recommendation.title: Accept after docs and checks
recommendation.body: Require public docs, a clean exact-head check run, and maintainer security acceptance, then continue with this overlay design.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history across the exec approval and gateway/node security-policy paths touched by this PR.
